nodes.name: Pt electrodissolution
nodes.procedure: To prepare the Pt stock solution, we used an electrodissolution technique with the standard electrochemical setting, using 99.99% Pt wire as the working electrode in 0.5 M H2SO4 as electrolyte. Cyclic voltammetry was performed by applying a broad bias range to the Pt working electrode (0.4 - 1.8 V, 50 mV s^-1, 1810 cycles), in order to induce the cyclic oxidation and reduction of its surface, upon which Pt^{2+} ions were slowly dissolved into the electrolyte.

nodes.name: Pt electrodeposition on MoS2
nodes.procedure: The support consists of single- and few-layer MoS2 crystals, grown by Chemical Vapor Deposition on the surface of a bulk graphite crystal. Electrodeposition of Pt on 2D MoS2 crystals was performed in a three-electrode single compartment cell, with Pt counter and Ag/AgCl reference electrodes, while the 2D MoS2/graphite support was set as the working electrode. The as-produced electrolyte, containing auxiliary ligand-free Pt ions (≈1 mg L^-1), was used. By depositing small amounts of Pt under specific conditions (e.g., CV: +0.3 V to -0.3 V vs RHE, 2 mV s^-1, 3 cycles; CP: 500 mA cm^-2, 1 s), we aimed for a high-density decoration of the whole MoS2 basal plane with ultrafine Pt particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt bilayers show sizeable energy gap of ≈0.3 eV with fully suppressed LDOS near Fermi energy, evidencing nonmetallic/semiconducting nature. Gap observed in all 12 investigated particles, varying between 0.3-0.4 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We have performed tunneling spectroscopy measurements to resolve the fine details of the LDOS of Pt bilayers... The most striking feature, was a sizeable energy gap of ≈0.3 eV, with fully suppressed Pt LDOS near the Fermi energy (0 V), evidencing the nonmetallic nature of the electronic structure of Pt bilayers (Figure 1c).
